summary: The integration, checker, configuration and scientific-summary changes at c817d225 meet the agreed scope. The catalog checker is now independent of where the repository sits on disk: it finds the root by source-tree markers or takes --repository. It dispatches analysis per profile, so a subset catalog validates without the original five entries, and unknown schema, kind and analysis values fail. Path-escape, symlink, hash and size checks are in place. Relocation verification checks destination and frozen hashes, executable bits, the 359 original additions, exact frozen-archive coverage and, with --source-git, closure over transitive notes-root references. Recomputing the four measured populations gives 156+54+18+12 = 240 rows, matching the logs. The campaign reports keep the required scientific limits. C++: count 1 spans five OSTs and 11.42 GiB/s is a reader rate, not a storage ceiling. SDF uses four BDs in total, while Perlmutter uses four BDs per GPU with a different core policy, and the two sites are not pooled. The SDF replay is derivative and eight inputs are missing. The cube entry is pending with zero full cases; the failed bootstrap is kept only as a diagnostic, the prepared stripe count is 2 and there is no numerical-reference correctness claim. PR187/208 remaining-loop equivalence is unresolved, and the +2.14 s / +3.34 s figures match pr187_pr208.md. PR299 keeps uncontrolled cache, C1 unfixed at acfd029 and Run77 deferred. Status labels are honest: the GPU scaling record says independent results review was not performed, and the stripe screen says it is pending. Packaging and lint exclusions cover every new source-only path. The committed logs match the supplied validation evidence. There is one low, non-blocking hardening note.

Read the C++, psana stripe, GPU scaling, SDF, cube, PR299 and multi-site reports and the GPU scaling manifest; the scientific limits in scope are all present and correctly labelled.

Byte identity of the 1612 frozen files and 1631 source blobs was not independently recomputed; it relies on the cryptographic validation logs. Frozen sources were spot-checked only through the links in campaign reports.
Replay output artifacts are on scratch outside the repository and were not inspected.

Not every log was read: isolation-01, pr-import, pr299-verify, pr299-tests, pr187-tests, catalog-final and replay-01 were accepted from the embedded evidence, and the full dependency-closure.json and relocation.json contents were not enumerated.
Did not re-read the PR187/208 SDF wrapper README, docs/performance/README.md, FORMAT.md, templates, or the archive README in full.

findings.evidence: In check_sdf the paired-speedup controls are built as a dict keyed only by repeat: {r['repeat']: rate for r in group if r['gpus'] == '1'}. Uniqueness is enforced only on (cohort, case). So if two one-GPU rows for the same medium shared a repeat value, the dict would silently overwrite one of them, leaving the README paired-speedup check sound only on current data. The per-cell n check and the table comparison make this unlikely to hide a real error today.
findings.requested_change: Optional hardening: before building the dict, require that the (media, gpus, repeat) keys are unique within the 45028778 full rows, matching the duplicate guards in the other profiles.
